effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per rule of the Mantle specification's Channel Operations section (ordering, sequencing, bridging, then payload, proof, gas, validation and execution of each of the five operations), in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-ledger that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml: 1.98.1 at the audited tag, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (annotated tag 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c, which peels to commit f76be2dde171711299eb9c25ec7cc6a3821fe240); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot); the other operation families and the Mantle Ledger section are audited by their own briefs.

The section covers message ordering, decentralized sequencing (the round-robin sequencer selection and its starting slot), bridging, and the five operations CHANNEL_INSCRIBE, CHANNEL_CONFIG, CHANNEL_DEPOSIT, CHANNEL_WITHDRAW and CHANNEL_TRANSFER, each with payload, proof, execution gas, validation and execution rules, and a worked example. Its requirements are every numbered or stated rule under those headings, including the gas figures and the example's expected values.

Where the section lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/channel.rs and src/mantle/channel_notes.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): channel identity, configuration (accredited keys, threshold), sequencer state and the round_robin function, channel-registered notes. src/mantle/ops/op.rs: the five channel operation payloads. ops/signed_op.rs, ops/signed_operation.rs, ops/signed_op_error.rs, ops/proof_zk_and_ed.rs: the signature and proof carried by a channel operation. core/src/proofs/channel_multi_sig_proof.rs: the multi-signature proof CHANNEL_CONFIG, CHANNEL_WITHDRAW and CHANNEL_TRANSFER use. src/mantle/fixtures/channel.rs: how tests build channels. The per-operation validation and execution code is in core/src/mantle/ops/channel/ (inscribe.rs, config.rs, deposit.rs, withdraw.rs, channel_transfer.rs, verification.rs); it is outside the unit's listed paths but is where most of the section's rules are carried out, so trace rows may cite it and proofs may exercise it.
- ledger/src/mantle/mod.rs and src/mantle/helpers.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): validation and execution of each channel operation against the ledger state, including note re-creation on deposit and note unregistration on withdraw.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; core/src/mantle/fixtures/ shows how transactions and ledgers are built in tests. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
